title: Release Pipeline Validation failed
body:
Release Pipeline Validation workflow failed.

@podman-container-tools/podman-maintainers PTAL

**Workflow run:** https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/33587258974

**Failed jobs:**
- validate-tokens: success
- build-artifacts-main: failure
- build-artifacts-latest-branch: success

comments.body:
@ashley-cui PTAL

```
make ARCH=aarch64 notarize &> /dev/null
```

Why are we running without any output?
So all we have is exit code 2 with no error to know why things failed.

@Luap99 Historically because the this is the step that deals with our signing key. GHA does its best effort to block out any information that might be a secret but we erase output just in case. 

Anyhow, I'll take a look and see if I can find out why this failed.

Ack, yeah we certainly need to be careful to not leak the key in logs. But would the commands we run actually write any secret to stdout/err? That would be seem like a bad default.
Github logs by default will already have logic to hide secrets from the output logs, so anything defined as secret will be redacted by default making leaks unlikely.

Anyhow I guess we could wait if it fails tomorrow again. Also since we make a release at the moment I guess we will see if it passes there on 6.1 or not.

It looks like just a flake, I [re-ran](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/actions/runs/33587258974) the job and it seemed to pass. The nightly run on the 6.1 branch passed too, I think we can just ignore this. I haven't seen this flake before, so it seems pretty rare, but if it happens again, I'll add a re-try or something to the validation pipeline.

Re logs: Let me test it locally and see if the command does output any secrets, I think this was just an additional precaution.
